sentences.text:
Mrs. S.R. Sahoo, Asc
 Coram:
 Justice G. Satapathy
 Order(Oral)
Order No. 16.01.2024
 02. 1.

This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual /Physical Mode).
2.

This is a bail application U/S.439 of Cr.P.C. by the petitioner for grant of bail in connection with Sonepur P.S. Case No. 216 of 2022 corresponding to S.C. Case No.20/06 of 2023 pending in the Court of learned Addl. Sessions Judge, Sonepur for commission of offences punishable under Sections 366/376(1)/323 of the IPC, on the allegation of kidnapping the victim and committing rape upon her.
3. Heard, Mr. B. Karna, learned counsel for the Petitioner and Mrs. S.R. Sahoo, learned ASC in the matter and perused the record.
4. It appears from the record that the Petitioner is in custody since 13.11.2022, but no witness has yet been examined even after framing of charge against the Petitioner on 27.06.2023.

This Court,
therefore, obviously considers that the conclusion of trial would certainly take some more time.

5. In the aforesaid situation and taking into consideration the nature and gravity of accusations raised against the Petitioner and the examination of witness having not done, even after more than 7 months of framing of charge against the Petitioner, this Court admits the Petitioner to bail.

6. Hence, the bail application of the petitioner stands allowed and the petitioner is allowed to go on bail on furnishing bail bonds of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand) only with two solvent sureties for the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned Court in seisin of the case on such terms and Subal @ Saroj Bag vs State Of Orissa ...

1 conditions as deem fit and proper by it with following conditions:-
(i) the petitioner shall not commit any offence while on bail,
(ii) the petitioner shall attend the trial Court on each date of posting without fail unless his attendance is dispensed with.
(iii) the petitioner shall not leave the jurisdiction of the trial Court without prior permission till disposal of the case.

It is clarified that the Court in seisin of the case will be at liberty to cancel the bail of the petitioner without further reference to this Court, if any of the above conditions are violated or a case for cancellation of bail is otherwise made out.

In the wake of aforesaid, the subsequent involvement of the petitioners in future for grave and serious offences on prima facie accusations may be treated as a ground for cancellation of bail in this case.

7. Accordingly, the BLAPL stands disposed of.
8.
Issue urgent certified copy of the order as per Rules.
